scope.description: Same four-phase scenario as the executed revision (A and B bootstrapped, A snapshots, C shut down for its own removal, RemoveServer C committed, then either two further commits or none depending on the case, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs or without it, C brought back and caught up, B partitioned, one Apply on the leader), with a third case restore_on_shallow that omits the two extra commits. The probe records the staged commit index before each restart and the resulting configuration, peer count and write outcome in every case.
assumptions: The staged commit index only advances when a log entry is dispatched, so omitting the extra commits leaves it below the removal entry's index; the observation records the staged value (5 in the shallow case against 7 in the failing case) so the difference is inspectable.
The shallow case is otherwise identical in operations, stores and transports, so the only difference is whether the removal entry falls inside the replayed prefix.
excluded: No control is added for the shallow case beyond comparing it with the failing case and the flag-off case, which already exist in the same execution.

basis.prefix: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real shutdown of C, real RemoveServer, real commits (two, or none in the shallow case), real restart of A on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real restart of C, real partition. No fabricated state; the shallow case only omits ordinary client commits.

comparisons.description: A restarted leader must not count a voter whose removal is committed in its own log (failing case).
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the committed membership.
A write whose Apply reported success must be held by a quorum of the configuration committed in the log.
Control: with the committed membership the same partition must make the leader refuse the write.
Boundary: with the removal entry above the replayed prefix the restart must keep the committed membership and must not resurrect the removed voter.

before.description: Three-voter in-process cluster {A,B,C} at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts. A snapshots, then C is shut down for its own removal, RemoveServer C commits with {A,B}, two further commands push the persisted commit index past the removal entry, and A is restarted on the same stores with RestoreCommittedLogs (case restore_on) or without it (control restore_off). The restarted A's configuration and peer count are observed against B's. Then C is brought back on its old stores so it catches up from A, B is partitioned from A, and one Apply is issued on A; the probe records whether the Apply succeeded, the entry index, A's commit and applied indexes, whether the entry reached B, and the FSM lengths on both sides.
assumptions: C is offline for its own removal, so it never learns it was removed; that is an ordinary operator sequence (a failed node is removed while down and then comes back).
B and C both hold every entry up to the removal, so the entries, commit index and configurations come from real replication.
After the partition, {A,B} is the configuration committed in the log (removal entry committed), so an entry present only on A cannot be committed.
excluded: No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the explicit disconnection of B.
The probe does not assert what happens after the partition heals, which is the subject of the dual-majority harness.

prefix.before: Real bootstrap of all three voters, real snapshot, real RemoveServer, real commits, real shutdown/restart of the leader and of the removed voter on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real transport reconnection and real partition. No fabricated configuration or log state.
prefix.after: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real shutdown of C, real RemoveServer, real commits (two, or none in the shallow case), real restart of A on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real restart of C, real partition. No fabricated state; the shallow case only omits ordinary client commits.

before.description: A restarted leader must not count a voter whose removal is committed in its own log.
Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the committed membership.
An entry whose Apply reported success on the stale-membership leader must be present on a quorum of the configuration committed in the log ({A,B} requires both members).

Control: the same restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the committed membership.
A write whose Apply reported success must be held by a quorum of the configuration committed in the log.
Control: with the committed membership the same partition must make the leader refuse the write.
Boundary: with the removal entry above the replayed prefix the restart must keep the committed membership and must not resurrect the removed voter.

revision_reason: Adds a third case to the same scenario that pins the trigger boundary: in the shallow case the two commits that push the persisted commit index past the removal entry are omitted, so the removal entry stays above the replayed prefix. Existing cases, observations and comparisons are unchanged; one comparison is added for the shallow case, where the committed membership must be kept.
